audit.whatIsWrong: Nevermove is the ability the whole early game is built around — named in nine strings — and the entry never says when it roots. It calls it "the lazy double-bird root" and tells the reader to "sidestep the E" and "do NOT walk in a straight line at him", which describes dodging the outgoing wave.
audit.why: Riot's Nevermove text: "Swain launches a wave of demonic power forward. It then returns to Swain and roots enemies it hits. Swain can then choose to pull all rooted champions closer." The outgoing wave does nothing. The root is on the RETURN pass, travelling back toward Swain. That inverts the timing completely: the safe moment is the instant it goes past you, and the dangerous one is a beat later when it comes home — so the correct play is to step in behind it, not to dodge sideways when it is thrown. A reader taught to sidestep the throw walks straight into the return every time. The pull that follows a landed root is also never mentioned, and it is what sets up Vision of Empire.
audit.corrected: The return-pass root and the follow-up pull written into spikes[0], early, mid, wants.you[0], wants.foe[0], whys[0], whys[1], tldr, winCon, phases[1].why, breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[2], dontsFull[1] and report[5], with the real 12s rank-1 cooldown.

audit.whatIsWrong: Death's Hand is referred to only as "Q poke" and "his single Q poke". Its stacking mechanic is never mentioned, and phases[0].why claims "Empowered-hit weaving wins the early AA exchanges" at a stage the chart gives to Swain.
audit.why: Riot's text: "Swain unleashes several bolts of eldritch power that pierce through enemies. Enemies hit take more damage for each bolt they are struck by." It is not one poke of fixed size — it is a fan of bolts whose damage depends on how many of them clip you, which is a function of how square-on and how close you are. That makes it the reason Ambessa cannot walk straight at him at level 1, and it is also on a 7s cooldown falling to 3s, the shortest in the matchup.
audit.corrected: Written into early, phases[0].why, breakdown.cooldowns and report[5].

audit.whatIsWrong: Demonic Ascension is the page's tracked ability, and its defining property is stated nowhere. mid says "Demonic Ascension drains a lot, so you must commit your full burst"; dosFull[0] says "Only engage once it is down or baited". wants.foe[1] also says "Stack Demonic Ascension (R) souls", attributing soul fragments to the ultimate.
audit.why: Riot's text: "This form is indefinite as long as Swain drains enemy champions." You cannot wait it out while standing in it — the timer only runs while no champion is in range, so the answer is to leave the 650-unit radius, not to out-last it. And the soul fragments belong to Ravenous Flock, the passive, with Vision of Empire granting one per champion hit; Demonic Ascension does not collect them.
audit.corrected: The indefinite-while-draining rule written into mid, dosFull[0], dontsFull[0], breakdown.cooldowns and report[5]; soul fragments reattributed to Ravenous Flock in wants.foe[1], late and dontsFull[2].

audit.whatIsWrong: late credits "your R's passive armor-pen healing", mid says to "W-brace his bomb so it amps your next slam", and spikes[2] says Public Execution "suppresses through any peel".
audit.why: Three separate problems. Public Execution has no armour penetration and no healing. Repudiation's bonus goes to Repudiation's own slam — Riot's text says "this ability will deal increased damage" — not to Sundering Slam, so bracing and then saving the slam throws the bonus away. And "suppresses through any peel" is an unfalsifiable claim about abilities not in this matchup; the verifiable and better reason is that Swain has no dash in his kit at all, so the gap-close cannot be answered.
audit.corrected: All three replaced: the burst reason becomes Ravenous Flock's healing being out-paced, the brace bonus lands on Repudiation's own slam, and the ultimate's value is stated as Swain's total lack of mobility.

The chart also gives Swain level 1 while whys[0] says "neither side wins", and gives him level 6 while whys[4] says his kit "has no escape from the gap-close and lockdown".

The packet levelChart is Skill, Skill, Ambessa, Ambessa, Ambessa, Ambessa, Ambessa, which matches the prose: even early because Swain is immobile and Ambessa has one ability, then Ambessa's from 3 onward.
audit.corrected: diffRating lowered from 7.5/10 to 4.5/10, with breakdown.difficulty and the Final Matchup Rating row matched. Level 1 flipped to Skill in both layers. Level 6 should also read Ambessa but "Swain" (5 characters) to "Ambessa" (7) crosses the band, and the diff label should move from TRICKY to FAV, which crosses it too — both documented in notes.

audit.whatIsWrong: phases[1].why repeats the champion-wide "Dash-resets stack your passive shield mid-trade" error, and not one cooldown number appears in either layer even though the whole page is organised around tracking Demonic Ascension.
audit.why: Drakehound's Step grants no shield — it grants the next attack bonus range, damage and attack speed plus an energy refund, and Repudiation is Ambessa's only shield. And the spike shape here is entirely a cooldown story that was never told: Nevermove is 12s at rank 1 and barely moves across its ranks, Death's Hand collapses from 7s to 3s so his poke gets relentless as he levels, Vision of Empire is 22s, and Demonic Ascension is a flat 120s whose duration does not tick down while he is draining a champion. That last point is why the ultimate is a positioning problem rather than a timing one, and it changes what "wait it out" means at every stage from 6 onward.
audit.corrected: phases[1].why corrected to name what the passive actually does, and the real numbers written into spikes[0], early, breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[0], dosFull[2] and report[5].

Each other entry has an equally concrete answer available.

notes:
THREE PACKET FALSE POSITIVES on this matchup: suspectNames flags "Demonic Ascension's" (spikes[3]), "Stack Demonic Ascension" (wants.foe[1]) and "Once Sundering Slam" (whys[3]). All three ability names are spelled correctly; the distances come from the possessive and the leading words. wants.foe[1] did have a real error, but a different one — it credited soul-fragment collection to the ultimate when it belongs to Ravenous Flock.

The Nevermove return-pass rule is the finding. Nine strings tell the reader to dodge an ability whose harmless half is the one they are dodging. Riot's text is explicit that the wave roots on the way back to Swain, which means stepping in behind the outgoing wave is safe and the reflex to jump sideways when he throws it is what gets you rooted.
